verdict_basis: I tried to break the command-specific end-note policy with fresh valid wrong-family, tab-separated, compact, and spaced ordinary note terminators across CLASS and DESCRIPTION inputs. The decisive ownership probes all pass at Rust revision 082981d14ae7cc1e177c9437f38da296f44b4031: wrong-family end hnote/end rnote remain payload, a literal tab between end and note closes the block, and later declarations remain visible. Two DESCRIPTION attached-note controls still fail, but the same width-and-text-position drift reproduces with both spaced and compact ordinary terminators, so it does not falsify the end-grammar mechanism under review.

java: CommandFactoryNote keeps ordinary floating notes on END = ^[%s]*end[%s]?note$, so wrong-family end hnote/end rnote lines remain payload and any single PlantUML whitespace, including a tab, can separate end from note.
CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity uses the same ordinary END matcher for attached notes and reserves the brace-only END_WITH_BRACKET matcher for the alternate bracket form.
rust: At 082981d1, parse/mod.rs note_command_parts strips sequence-only prefixes but completed_multiline_note_payload only consults the broader note-family terminator set when the opener is sequence-shaped (left/right/over/across without of). Ordinary note-as and ordinary attached note forms now stay on is_ordinary_note_terminator.

is_ordinary_note_terminator checks the post-end separator with char::is_whitespace, so a literal tab terminator is accepted by the same helper used by dispatch masking and by the class/deployment multiline consumers.
prohibited_pattern_audit: A targeted git grep for the fresh stems and mechanism name found no fixture-shaped conditionals in shipping Rust files.
No new parity-specific constants or comparator edits were introduced by the held-outs; the residual DESCRIPTION failure is a geometry delta in an already-rendered attached note.

Rust and Java both retain end rnote as display text and only close on endnote, with the later artifact still present.

The block closes and the later artifact survives, but the no-oracle renderer draws the attached note narrower than Java and shifts the second text row left. This is geometry residue, not a terminator-ownership failure.
